findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an ADR (or named design-doc target) capturing the coordinator architecture, the core/adapter retry-ownership split, and the rationale for replacing the rolling 5-of-10 breaker with the three-consecutive scoped fuse.
evidence: 'Finish expand/contract cutover, remove legacy retry/write fallbacks, and seal manifests, observability, cursor behavior, documentation'
'Remove the rolling 5-of-10 breaker. An endpoint family opens after three consecutive exhausted eligible logical outcomes'
'Build one provider-neutral coordinator around immutable observation and pure per-ticket TicketPlan values'
findings.finding: The plan makes a significant architectural decision (a new provider-neutral coordinator with pure TicketPlan values and the replacement of the rolling 5-of-10 breaker with a three-consecutive scoped fuse) but does not commit to an explicit ADR/design-doc capturing this decision; it only references generic 'documentation' sealing in slice 5.
scenarios: A future maintainer needs to understand why the breaker changed from rolling 5-of-10 to a three-consecutive scoped fuse and why core/adapter retry ownership was split.
findings.suggested_fix: Name a specific ADR deliverable in slice 5 (e.g., 'ADR: coordinator boundary + scoped-fuse policy') rather than generic 'documentation'.

scenarios: A newly cut-over operation family misbehaves in production and operators need to revert quickly without shipping a new build.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify the multi-scope 'fuse' (endpoint-family / two-families-for-provider / tenant / global) against prior art: cite the standard circuit-breaker taxonomy (consecutive-failure vs rate-based) and the repo's existing blast-radius breaker (jira-sync-setup.md, ADR 0028) it replaces, stating why the new scoped topology is preferred over a single-level consecutive-failure breaker.
evidence: Plan: 'Remove the rolling 5-of-10 breaker. An endpoint family opens after three consecutive exhausted eligible logical outcomes across at least two tickets. Provider scope additionally requires two endpoint families.'
Web (Level Up / GeeksforGeeks): circuit breakers ship in resilience libraries with both consecutive-failure and rate-based variants (Polly, Hystrix) — a well-trodden pattern.

Repo: docs/jira-sync-setup.md:642-648 and ADR 0028 describe the current blast-radius breaker and cite prior art (Argo allowEmpty, Entra deletion threshold); the plan neither references nor contrasts with it.
ABSENCE: the plan states no rationale for why this multi-level scope escalation topology is preferable to a standard single-level consecutive-failure breaker.
findings.finding: The plan replaces the existing rolling 5-of-10 breaker with a novel multi-scope 'fuse' (endpoint family opens after three consecutive exhausted eligible outcomes across two tickets; provider scope additionally requires two endpoint families; plus tenant/global scopes) but cites no prior art — neither the established circuit-breaker taxonomy (consecutive-failure vs rate-based breakers, e.g. Polly/Hystrix) nor the repo's own accepted breaker design, which itself grounds its threshold in prior art (Argo allowEmpty, Entra deletion threshold, per docs/jira-sync-setup.md and ADR 0028).
findings.location: Approved policy — 'Remove the rolling 5-of-10 breaker. An endpoint family opens after three consecutive exhausted eligible logical outcomes across at least two tickets. Provider scope additionally requires two endpoint families.'
scenarios: Reviewers/implementers cannot tell whether the multi-scope escalation is a justified improvement or an ad-hoc re-invention of an existing, documented breaker.
The new fuse silently discards the prior-art grounding (Argo/Entra) that the removed breaker carried.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short 'Prior art' note to Approved policy referencing the existing blast-radius breaker (ADR 0028 / jira-sync-setup.md, incl. its Argo allowEmpty / Entra threshold provenance) and the standard consecutive-failure breaker pattern, then state the specific reason (per-endpoint isolation + provider-wide safety) the multi-scope escalation is chosen over reusing/extending the existing single-level breaker.
